stem: Before the next dispensing, a retail collaborative agreement purports to let the pharmacist prescribe alprazolam and methylphenidate. Select all supported conclusions.

choices.text: In this setting, professional liability insurance waives the schedule restriction.
At this stage, only Schedule II is prohibited; Schedule IV is allowed.
On this record, the agreement cannot authorize retail pharmacist prescribing of Schedule II through V substances.
For this scenario, the controlled-substance limitation applies even if the supervising physician signs the agreement.
Schedule VI prescribing can be authorized only within the separate statutory retail CDTM limits.
